title: Negotiated kernel adapter and attention buffer coalescer for mixed-precision paths
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Goal: Implement a negotiated kernel adapter that performs a lightweight runtime "precision handshake" between INT8/FP8 candidate kernels and an attention buffer coalescer that minimizes host/device copies during prefill and decode. Background: Current runtime often incurs per-layer dequant/cast overhead and extra memory copies when switching precision or when attention KV slices are non-contiguous. This ticket combines a negotiation layer (small policy engine + microbenchmarks) with a buffer coalescing stage that produces a contiguous, staging window for attention kernels, enabling zero-copy or single-copy paths for both prefill and decode. Approach:
- Kernel negotiation: add a tiny runtime scorer that samples microbenchmarks (per-model shape, sequence-length bucket) and picks a pair of compatible kernels (int8/fp8) with lowest expected p99 latency for the next N tokens. The scorer will favor zero-copy-compatible kernels when possible.
- Precision handshake: introduce a compact metadata token that kernels advertise (casting/-inplace capability, kv-layout, required alignment) so the adapter can avoid unnecessary host-side casts.
- Attention buffer coalescer: when KV slices are fragmented (mixed microbatches or interleaved windows), coalesce into a staging slab on-device with minimal allocation churn; keep a reusable slab keyed by shape+precision. The coalescer will also attempt head-slicing to reuse cached tensor memory for repeated prefixes.
- Copy-avoidant path: for kernels that support in-place cast or fused cast+matmul, route requests through an inlined path; fall back to single-copy staging when unsupported.
Benchmarks & targets: initial microbench on A100-80GB with Llama-3-70B-ish sim: target p50 < 6ms for 8-token decode and p99 < 35ms on single-stream with INT8 fused kernels. Expected improvements: 6-12% end-to-end per-token latency reduction and 10-18% GPU memory allocation churn reduction for mixed-precision workloads. Observability: emit negotiation decisions to runtime telemetry (kernel_id, scorer_score, chosen_path) for later analysis.
Tradeoffs & risks: adds small policy complexity and a new slab allocator which needs runtime GC if shapes explode. There is a correctness risk when mixing kernels that have subtle fp8 exponent scaling differences — add a regression eval suite using our eval harness and a Monte-Carlo prompt set.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Negotiation API + scorer implemented and feature flagged. 2) Coalescer integrated with runtime slab allocator and reused across requests. 3) Microbench results show p50/p99 improvements versus baseline for mixed-precision traffic in perf harness. 4) End-to-end conformance tests (numerical drift thresholds) pass.
Artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUNTIME/pages/Hybrid+Kernel+Adapter; reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4321; perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/permix/kernel-negotiator.
Next steps: prototype scorer + per-shape slab (spike, 3 days), add telemetry hooks (1 day), run perf sweeps and iterate on tie-breaker heuristics (2 days).
